security_spec.violation_condition: FreeBSD kernel executing on a hart that implements Smaclic/Ssaclic without Smaiae (IMSIC) reads the CSR-based stopi/sclaimi registers in the trap handler to claim external interrupts; these CSRs do not exist on such a system, so the read returns zero, causing the kernel to silently drop all external interrupts routed through the ACLIC
security_spec.summary: Smaclic/Ssaclic no longer depends on Smaiae, so ACLIC-only harts lack IMSIC CSRs; FreeBSD's intr handler reading stopi/sclaimi gets zero → all external interrupts silently lost

findings.finding: Trap handler reads scause from the trapframe (saved by exception.S assembly), then delegates to intr_irq_handler(). No CSR-based stopi/sclaimi read is performed. The external interrupt is dispatched through the PIC framework, which uses memory-mapped I/O for claiming.
Same pattern as do_trap_supervisor: reads scause from trapframe, no CSR-based stopi/sclaimi reads. Delegates to intr_irq_handler() for external interrupts.

The local interrupt controller handler extracts the interrupt code from scause (saved in the trapframe), not from stopi/sclaimi CSRs. The sepc-saved scause is the standard privileged-spec CSR, always present. SIE_SEIE manipulation via intc_enable_intr/intc_disable_intr uses standard sie CSR bits (not AIA-specific bits), which work correctly in both legacy CLINT and ACLIC-direct modes.

The APLIC interrupt handler claims interrupts by reading the memory-mapped APLIC_IDC_CLAIMI register via bus_read_4() (aplic_read macro expands to bus_read_4 on sc->mem_res). This is a memory-mapped I/O register at offset 0x1C within the APLIC IDC structure, NOT a CSR read. It works correctly regardless of whether Smaiae (IMSIC) is present. The CLAIMI read returns zero when no interrupt is pending, correctly terminating the claim loop.

The APLIC driver explicitly rejects IMSIC configurations (Smaiae) via the 'msi-parent' property check, falling back to direct mode only. This is the correct behavior for the scenario described in the spec: APLIC in direct mode without IMSIC. The driver never attempts to use CSR-based stopi/sclaimi because it only supports direct mode.

sbi_ipi_intr() clears SIP_SSIP via csr_clear(sip, SIP_SSIP) at line 106. This register is cleared via the SBI IPI mechanism, not via ACLIC. In an ACLIC-direct system, software interrupts (SSI) still arrive through scause=1 because S-mode SSI is a local interrupt, not routed through the external interrupt controller. The SIP_SSIP clearing is the standard RISC-V mechanism and is correct for any system regardless of AIA extensions: SSI is a per-hart local interrupt, not platform-level.

IPI sending uses sbi_send_ipi() which calls into OpenSBI. OpenSBI's IPI path is separate from the external interrupt controller and uses the CLINT/ACLINT MSWI mechanism or SBI IPI extension. This is independent of whether the platform uses PLIC or APLIC for device interrupts.

SIE_SEIE (1 << 9) is defined as the standard supervisor external interrupt enable bit. This is part of the base privileged spec (always present) and is distinct from any AIA-specific sie bits. No stopi/sclaimi CSR definitions exist in this header.
The PLIC driver claims interrupts via memory-mapped PLIC_CONTEXT_CLAIM register (bus_read_4). No CSR reads at all. This works on any system regardless of AIA extensions.

The VMM APLIC emulation checks pending interrupts by scanning the virtual APLIC software state (aplic_irq structures), not by reading CSRs. The VMM never reads stopi/sclaimi CSRs for its guest interrupt injection logic.
